entry.title: Service Layer: cannot unblock contact-level marketing (BlockSendingMarketingContent / ContactEmploye
entry.content:
Environment: SAP Business One 10.0 for SAP HANA, version 10.00.191, FP 2202 (64-bit). Service Layer v1 (/b1s/v1).

Context: We manage the contacts of a business partner (ContactEmployees) through the Service Layer. The marketing block is set per contact, using the communication media rows (Email = CommunicationMediaId -1, Fax = -2, from table OCMM).

What works:

  • Creating a contact with the Email row Choose = tYES, and BlockSendingMarketingContent tYES (or absent): the contact is created and blocked.
  • Creating a contact with no block: works.
  • Updating other contact fields (name, position, active) with a partial PATCH on the business partner: works.

What fails: Unblocking a contact that is currently blocked (tYES to tNO). I tried these variants of PATCH /b1s/v1/BusinessPartners('CFR495302820'):

  1. Partial PATCH, only the contact, Email row set to tNO, without the replace header: {"ContactEmployees":[{"InternalCode":2268,"Name":"Buyer","Position":"...","ContactEmployeeBlockSendingMarketingContents":[{"CommunicationMediaId":-1,"Choose":"tNO","ContactEmployeeAbsEntry":2268}]}]} Result: HTTP 400, -5002 Internal error (-5002) occurred.

  2. Same as 1, plus "BlockSendingMarketingContent":"tNO" on the contact: same result (-5002).

  3. Same as 1, with both Email (-1) and Fax (-2) rows set to tNO, plus BlockSendingMarketingContent tNO: HTTP 400, -5002.

  4. Full ContactEmployees list with header B1S-ReplaceCollectionsOnPatch: true, Email row set to tNO for the target contact: HTTP 400, -1116 Could not commit transaction: Error -2035 detected during transaction.

  5. Partial PATCH with an empty array for ContactEmployeeBlockSendingMarketingContents: no error, but the block stays active.

A GET on the same contact returns: "BlockSendingMarketingContent": "tYES", "ContactEmployeeBlockSendingMarketingContents": [ {"ContactEmployeeAbsEntry": 2268, "CommunicationMediaId": -1, "Choose": "tYES", "CardCode": "...", "ContactPersonName": "Buyer"} ]

The same GET also shows a row under another contact (InternalCode 877) that points to contact 2268. The SAP GUI shows that other contact as not blocked.

Questions:

  1. What is the correct Service Layer request to change a contact's Email marketing block from tYES to tNO?
  2. Must the ContactEmployeeBlockSendingMarketingContents rows be replaced through the collection, and if so, how?
  3. Is there a known issue with -5002 / -2035 on contact marketing blocks in FP 2202?
  4. Is ContactEmployeeAbsEntry read-only in the Service Layer?

Thank you for any guidance.

entry.title: SAP B1 FP2602 - factur-x.xml overwrite issue
entry.content:
We are using SAP Business One 10.0 FP2602 on SQL Server and have implemented ZUGFeRD / Factur-X EN16931 using the "PDF with XML Attachment" electronic document protocol.


The Factur-X XML itself is generated correctly and the PDF can also be generated with the XML embedded.


The problem is the XML file name and the external XML storage.


For a valid Factur-X / ZUGFeRD PDF, the embedded XML attachment needs to remain named:
factur-x.xml


In our current configuration, the same file name is also used for the externally generated XML file in the configured XML folder.
So we currently get:
...\XML\factur-x.xml
for every invoice.


This is a serious problem for us because we have four locations/users that can create invoices at the same time. If several invoices are generated concurrently, all of them potentially write to the same physical file path and file name.
We therefore need a unique external path per invoice, while keeping the embedded attachment name inside the PDF as factur-x.xml.
The desired result would be something like:
...\XML\260053\factur-x.xml
...\XML\260054\factur-x.xml
...\XML\260055\factur-x.xml


while the embedded attachment in each PDF still remains:
factur-x.xml


According to the SAP Business One documentation, the field "File Name and Path" in the Electronic Documents Export Setup should support dynamic values / data source parameters and subfolders.
We therefore tested several variants in a test database.

We first tried:
[%OINV.DocNum]\factur-x.xml
but SAP created a literal folder named:
[%OINV.DocNum]

We then tried:
[%ODOC.DocNum]\factur-x.xml
but SAP again created a literal folder named:
[%ODOC.DocNum]

We also configured a User Query Category for the electronic document protocol.
As a test, we created the following query:
SELECT T0."DocNum"
FROM OINV T0
WHERE T0."DocEntry" = [%ODOC.DocEntry]

We also tried variants using [%ODOC.DocNum].
Depending on the query, either the parameter was still not resolved in the file path, or XML generation failed with:
Error - Cannot map all query parameters

We also tested using a query result alias such as:
SELECT T0."DocNum" AS "ZUGF_DOCNUM"
FROM OINV T0
WHERE T0."DocEntry" = [%ODOC.DocEntry]
and using:
[%ZUGF_DOCNUM]\factur-x.xml
but this was also treated literally and did not resolve to the invoice number.

If we leave the "File Name and Path" field empty, SAP automatically creates a uniquely named XML file such as:
RE_260053.xml

However, the same file name is then used inside the PDF attachment as well, so the PDF contains:
RE_260053.xml
instead of:
factur-x.xml

If we explicitly configure:
factur-x.xml
the PDF attachment name is correct, but all invoices use the same external XML file name.

So the issue is specifically that we seem to have only one file name setting controlling both:
the physical/external XML file name and the embedded XML attachment name inside the PDF

We need these two behaviors to be separated, or alternatively we need SAP to support a dynamic subfolder while keeping the file itself named factur-x.xml.


Has anyone successfully configured this with SAP Business One 10.0 FP2602 and the "PDF with XML Attachment" protocol?
Is there a correct syntax for dynamic paths with this protocol, for example:
<InvoiceNumber>\factur-x.xml

while keeping the attachment name inside the PDF as:
factur-x.xml
Or is this a known limitation or bug in FP2602?


If this has been corrected in a later patch level, SAP Note or hotfix, I would also appreciate the corresponding reference.


Thanks in advance.

entry.title: Period-end inventory cost recalculation for Moving Average items in SAP Business One 10.0 for HANA
entry.content:
Hi all,

Our customer runs SAP Business One 10.0 for HANA, and their items are valued using Moving Average.

Scenario we tested (item IT02, warehouse 01), in the order the documents were entered:

GRPO 887: Posting Date 01.09.26, entered 01.09.26, Qty +1, Cost 50.00
GRPO 888: Posting Date 02.09.26, entered 02.09.26, Qty +1, Cost 70.00
GRPO 889: Posting Date 03.09.26, entered 03.09.26, Qty +1, Cost 100.00
Goods Issue 174: Posting Date 01.09.26, entered 20.09.26, Qty -1, Cost 73.33

The Goods Issue was entered after the three receipts but backdated to 01.09.26. The system costed it at 73.33, which is the average at the time the document was created, not 50.00 as of the posting date. In the Inventory Audit Report sorted by posting date, the cumulative value goes negative (-23.33) at that line.

Our understanding is that SAP Business One uses perpetual moving average costing. The issue cost is fixed at the moment the document is created, based on the system transaction sequence, and the posting date does not affect it.

The customer expects a period-end "inventory recalculation" that re-costs past issues in posting-date order and posts the difference to a variance account.

Questions:
Can you confirm that standard SAP Business One (10.0, HANA) has no period-end recalculation or re-costing of Moving Average issues?
If so, is Inventory Revaluation the recommended way to correct the remaining stock value?
Are there any known add-ons or recommended practices for preventing or controlling backdated inventory transactions, besides approval procedures and period locking?

Thanks in advance.
